correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and exhaustive. For every binary word of lengths 1 through 7, the theta-conjugate set is constructed both from all cuts w=uv and independently from the defining equation qv=theta(v)w. The two constructions agree for every word. Direct reversal tests give maximum palindrome counts 2,2,2,2,2,2,3; at length 7 exactly 0100011 and 1011100 attain 3, with the explicit palindrome sets stated in the result.

value.rationale: The number three is not an arbitrary target: it is the conjectured global ceiling identified by the primary literature for ordinary palindromes in theta-conjugate sets. Determining the first binary Watson-Crick realization of that ceiling, and all shortest witnesses, gives a natural exact boundary attached directly to the open extremal problem. It also shortens the published attaining example from length 12 to the sharp minimum 7.
